summary: Configured node1 as the gateway for trusted 192.168.10.0/24 and guest 192.168.20.0/24 networks. Both receive DHCP, DNS, and NAT internet access. node2 serves infraset-trusted at app.home.test:8080; node4 can access it, while node3 is isolated.
actions_performed: Configured node1 WAN on eth1, trusted on eth2, guest on eth3, while preserving eth0 management access.
Added DHCP reservations, home.test DNS, WAN masquerading, and trusted/guest firewall zones.
Preferred the OpenWrt gateway and DNS on each client's private NIC.
Created and enabled the node2 HTTP service bound to 192.168.10.10:8080.
Verified trusted access, guest isolation, DNS, DHCP, and internet connectivity.

evidence.requirement: Gateway topology, NAT, and firewall policy
evidence.summary: node1 has active WAN, trusted, guest, and management interfaces; WAN masquerading is active, and only trusted/guest-to-WAN forwarding is permitted.

evidence.requirement: DHCP and DNS for both networks
evidence.summary: dnsmasq is running with leases 192.168.10.10 for node2, 192.168.10.20 for node4, and 192.168.20.10 for node3; clients received node1 as gateway and DNS with home.test search domain.

evidence.requirement: Internet access for trusted and guest clients
evidence.summary: node4 routed through 192.168.10.1 and node3 through 192.168.20.1; both resolved and fetched example.com successfully.
The enabled, active service listens only on 192.168.10.10:8080; node4 resolved app.home.test and received infraset-trusted.
node3 could resolve app.home.test but its HTTP connection was rejected, and it received no ping replies from trusted node4.
